title: Questa One Updated at DAC 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: At DAC 2026, Siemens EDA detailed how its Questa One verification platform now uses faster micro-service-connected engines, Anthropic's MCP, and an Agentic ToolKit to let AI agents auto-fix RTL and cut DFT simulation from weeks to days, while keeping engineers in the loop rather than pursuing full autonomy.

insights.claim: Siemens EDA's Questa One verification platform lets EDA engines communicate with each other bidirectionally via micro-services, which the company has also opened to AI agents by implementing Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP).
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: MCP adoption by a major EDA vendor signals MCP becoming a de facto interoperability standard for connecting AI agents to engineering tool chains, relevant for tracking Anthropic's enterprise and protocol traction beyond chatbots.
insights.quote: This also allowed Siemens to enable Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard created by Anthropic to let AI models connect to tools, files and databases.

insights.claim: In a demonstrated AI-driven lint-and-fix flow, an RTL netlist that produced 10,000 lint failures was auto-fixed and re-verified through a re-run of lint without a human in the loop.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A concrete productivity proof point (10,000 failures auto-remediated) that investors and customers can use to gauge real agentic-AI verification ROI versus marketing claims.
insights.locator: As an example consider the case of an RTL netlist

insights.claim: Combining Siemens' Tessent DFT (design-for-test) family with verification has compressed DFT simulation runtimes that previously took weeks down to just days.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude runtime reduction in DFT simulation is a concrete efficiency metric for evaluating EDA tool ROI on large SoC and chiplet projects.
insights.quote: DFT simulations that used to run for weeks are slimmed down to just days.

insights.claim: Complex electronic system product development can take three to four years, and design sizes are moving beyond traditional EDA tool capacity and performance limits, creating pressure for faster, higher-capacity verification engines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Frames the structural demand driver, design complexity outgrowing legacy EDA tools, behind AI-augmented EDA spending.
insights.locator: Abhi shared that complex electronic systems can take 3-4 years

insights.claim: Siemens' Questa One Agentic ToolKit (ATK) supplies domain-specific 'Context Intelligence' skills for RTL, lint, CDC, verification planning and debug that plug into orchestrators like Siemens' Coding Agent and Fuse Agent, while customers can substitute their own choice of agent.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: An open orchestration layer versus a closed agent stack is a competitive positioning choice; watch whether Siemens or rivals win developer mindshare via openness to third-party agents and models.
insights.quote: Customers can use Siemens agents or any other agent of their own choice. This is a partner approach, not just another EDA vendor.

insights.claim: MediaTek reports Questa One's LLM-agnostic methodology, which frequently uses NVIDIA NIM and Nemotron models for high-performance reasoning, has helped new engineers ramp up on RTL methodology faster.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Confirms NVIDIA's Nemotron and NIM models are being embedded as reasoning backends inside EDA agentic workflows, another distribution channel for NVIDIA's software stack beyond GPUs.
insights.quote: The Siemens methodology is LLM-agnostic, and allows engineers to leverage their choice of reasoning models. While Siemens frequently utilizes NVIDIA NIM and Nemotron for high-performance reasoning, the architecture is designed to be flexible

insights.claim: Siemens EDA has not reached fully autonomous IC design and verification that eliminates engineers; Questa One is instead framed as amplifying engineering judgment and productivity with a human-in-the-loop approach.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Tempers full-automation hype in EDA, a useful baseline for judging how far agentic AI has actually progressed in chip design versus vendor marketing.
insights.quote: Siemens has not reached fully autonomous IC design and verification to eliminate engineers, rather using Quest One will amplify engineering judgement and productivity.
insights.locator: Siemens has not reached fully autonomous

insights.claim: First-generation AI-based EDA tools were largely standalone point tools, but by 2026 AI is increasingly being used to orchestrate multiple EDA tools together to achieve higher-level design objectives.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Marks an inflection from point-tool AI to orchestration-layer AI in EDA, a framework for evaluating which EDA vendors are ahead on the orchestration layer.
insights.quote: The first generation of AI-based tools were basically point tools, but in 2026 the AI technology is being used to orchestrate other EDA tools to achieve higher-level objectives.
